end.summary:
Practised showing 11–20 as one bundle of ten and loose ones; some responses were right, but this was not steady yet.
Practised that the 1 in a teen number represents one ten; this is still building.
Saanvi often counted the bundle as 1 when finding the total, including examples with 2, 3, and 6 loose ones.
Saanvi counted on from ten for 14 and 16, but later read 15 as 1 and 5 making 6; the mix-up was not corrected after it was last seen.
end.parentNote: Asha practised teen numbers with bundles of ten, loose ones, and counting on from ten. Saanvi used counting on for 14 and 16; they still mixed up the bundle as one object and the 1 in 15 with one single stick, and this was not corrected after the last example. At home, make one bundle of 10 and add 1–9 loose objects, then ask, “How many altogether?” and have Saanvi say “one ten and ___ ones.”
